links.outcome: Model fairness metrics (BER, DP, EOD, EOP) across race, ethnicity, age, SES, and registry subgroups
links.effect: BER showed significant differences by registry (ratios >1.25 for all registries vs Seattle) but no significant bias by race, Hispanic ethnicity, age, or SES (BER ratio <1.25); DP, EOD, EOP insignificant.
links.quote: We observed significant differences in BER by registry, but no significant bias using the DP, EOD, and EOP metrics for socio-demographic or racial categories.

links.effect: Predictive accuracy differed between registries, with highest accuracy in the registry contributing the most data (Seattle); BER ratios for all registries >1.25.
links.quote: We found differences in predictive accuracy between registries, with the highest accuracy in the registry that contributed the most data (Seattle Registry, BER ratios for all registries >1.25).

screen.reason: The study directly evaluates algorithmic bias and fairness auditing metrics (demographic parity, equalized odds, equal opportunity) across protected subgroups and registries on retrospective electronic pathology reports.

primary.practice: algorithmic bias and fairness auditing across demographic and geographic subgroups
